characters.name: Victor Hatherley
characters.note: Young hydraulic engineer, narrator of his own ordeal; loses his thumb in the press at Eyford.

characters.name: Dr. Watson
characters.note: Narrator of the story, a doctor who treats Hatherley and brings him to Holmes.

characters.name: Colonel Lysander Stark
characters.note: Emaciated, German-accented criminal who operates the coining press; also called Fritz by Elise.

characters.name: Elise
characters.note: Stark's pretty foreign companion who warns Hatherley and helps him escape.

characters.name: Mr. Ferguson
characters.note: Stout Englishman with a chinchilla beard, Stark's manager and accomplice.

characters.name: Inspector Bradstreet
characters.note: Scotland Yard inspector who accompanies the party to Eyford.

characters.name: the guard
characters.note: Railway guard who brings Hatherley to Watson's door at dawn.

characters.name: the station-master
characters.note: Eyford station-master who reports the fire at Dr. Becher's house.

characters.name: the plain-clothes man
characters.note: Officer who accompanies Bradstreet and suggests the west.

characters.name: the porter
characters.note: Sleepy porter at Eyford station on the night Hatherley arrives.

characters.name: Jeremiah Hayling
characters.note: Hydraulic engineer from a year-old advertisement, probably a previous victim of the press; mentioned only.

characters.name: Dr. Becher
characters.note: Englishman whose house at Eyford burns; a name used by the criminals, mentioned only.

locations.name: Watson's consulting-room
locations.note: Watson's consulting room near Paddington Station in London.

locations.name: Victoria Street chambers
locations.note: Hatherley's professional chambers, where Stark calls on him.

locations.name: the house at Eyford
locations.note: Remote house near Eyford in Berkshire with the hydraulic press; burned down at the end.

locations.name: Eyford Station
locations.note: Small railway station in Berkshire where Hatherley arrives and later returns.

locations.name: the country road
locations.note: The long, jolting carriage route from Eyford Station to the house.

brief.place: London (Paddington, Baker Street, Victoria Street) and a remote, overgrown house near Eyford in Berkshire, near Reading, with a long gravel drive and a high road.
brief.dress: Victorian: Hatherley in a heather tweed suit and soft cap; Watson in a frock-coated doctor's dress; Holmes in a dressing-gown at home; Stark thin and plainly but neatly dressed; Elise in a rich dark dress; Ferguson stout with a chinchilla beard; Bradstreet in a Scotland Yard inspector's dress.
brief.buildings_and_objects: A dim, decaying old house with corridors, low doors, a stone-floored passage, a bedroom window about thirty feet over a garden, and a hydraulic press with an iron floor and descending wooden-walled chamber, lamps, a harmonium, German books, and a barred oak shutter. A hansom cab, a single chestnut horse, a closed carriage with frosted-glass windows, and an ordnance map.
depiction_rules: Show Hatherley's bandaged hand and the missing thumb accurately in scenes after the injury.
Stark should be drawn as gaunt and cadaverous, with sharpened nose and chin and taut cheeks.
Elise should be shown as frightened and beautiful, holding a lamp or candle.
Show the press as a huge descending ceiling in a small square chamber, not as a human-scale room.
Keep the fire and burned house visible only in the late scenes, with the roof having fallen in.
